<description>
`invalidateblock` returns `null` even when the block was not invalidated because the RPC does not pay attention to `Chainstate::InvalidateBlock()` return value. If there is a problem disconnecting the block (for example, the undo data is corrupt), the chain remains partially rolled back when telling the user that the operation succeeded. This creates an error in every failure case, including the genesis block case, and makes RPC look at the return value. The error reports a failed block and how far the chain was rolled back before the block returned.

Fixes #36546
</description>
